sections.title: Who gets what
sections.content: You know *ad* ("to give", Unit 16) and the ending *-nak/-nek* for the person who receives (Unit 12). The person takes *-nak/-nek* and the present takes the accusative *-t*. With a pronoun you know *nekem*, *neked*, *neki* (A1). *kap* ("to get", A1) turns it round: *Egy könyvet kapok.* To say what a present is for, *-ra/-re* works as in *éjszakára* (Unit 16): *karácsonyra* means "for Christmas".

sections.title: Giving and getting
rows: What are you giving Petra for Christmas?
I get a book for Christmas.

items.english: What are you giving Petra for Christmas?
I give you a bunch of flowers.
What are you getting for Christmas?

sections.content: The person is not the object: say *Anyának adok egy könyvet*, not *Anyát adok egy könyvet*. The thing you give takes *-t*; the person takes *-nak/-nek*.
